title: Compound Data: Tuples
goal: Group values of different types into a tuple and recognize the unit type.

sections.text: You often need to group a fixed number of values together without defining a full struct. A tuple combines multiple values of different types into one compound value.

sections.caption: Parentheses enclose both the type signature and the literal tuple.

sections.text: Tuple elements are accessed by position using dot notation with zero-based indices. You write `point.0` for the first item and `point.1` for the second.

sections.code:
let x = point.0;
let y = point.1;
sections.caption: Indexing uses dot syntax, not square brackets.

sections.text: An empty tuple `()` is a special type called the unit type. It has exactly one value, also written `()`.
Functions without an explicit return type arrow implicitly return `()`. A statement ending in a semicolon also evaluates to `()`.

explanation: Group values of different types into a tuple and recognize the unit type.
